title: When the church does wrong
hookLine: the church has harmed people; honesty, repentance and justice are required

lines: JUDGMENT BEGINS AT THE HOUSE OF GOD.
SAYING SO IS NOT AN ATTACK.
cards: Some hard words about the church are inside the Bible itself. A letter of Peter puts it flatly: "For the time is come that judgment must begin at the house of God." Not out there, with the outsiders.
At the house of God. It matters, because churches have harmed people. Abuse, and abuse covered up.
People shamed, driven out, told God was finished with them. Congregations that stood beside cruelty and called it order. Saying so out loud isn't an attack on faith.
The Bible sets the pattern for it.

teach.b: In year three, the line was believe them. This lesson asks what comes next. The Bible's word is repent, and it gives three pictures of what that looks like when a whole community has gone wrong.

First, honesty that says we. Daniel prays over the wrongs of his people. He doesn't point at them from a safe distance: "We have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled."
He stands inside the failure instead of beside it. Second, a turned life.
To people coming out to be baptized, John the Baptist says: "Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance." Fruit you can see.

In Luke, when people ask what to do, his answers are concrete: share your coat, take no more than you're owed, don't bully anyone with your power. Repentance shows up in how you act on Monday. Third, repair.

Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector, and rich, meets Jesus, and in his own house he stands up and says: "Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold."
Not just sorry. Paid back, and more. Churches have tried to walk this road, some with public confessions, apologies, investigations and payments to survivors.
Some have walked it well, some slowly, some not yet, and the people who were harmed are often the ones who can say how far it still has to go.
In these texts, judgment begins at the house of God. So does repentance.

how: Christians practice repentance through confession, private or in a liturgy, and churches of several traditions have made public confessions and apologies, opened independent investigations, and offered redress to people harmed by church leaders or institutions.

games.q: what does “when the church does wrong” mean?
o: a reason to stop speaking about faith at all
a private matter for leaders to settle quietly
honest confession, a turned life and real repair

games.q: repentance in the Bible — tap the pairs.

s: the Bible only criticizes outsiders, never God's own people
a letter of Peter says judgment must begin at the house of God.
Daniel confesses his people's wrongs as 'we', not 'they'
we have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled.
in these texts, repentance is just feeling sorry
John the Baptist asks for fruits meet for repentance, and Zacchaeus restores fourfold.

games.q: you're Zacchaeus, a rich tax collector, and Jesus has come to your house. people are muttering that he has gone to be the guest of a sinner. what do you do?
o: say nothing; the visit speaks for itself.
give half to the poor and pay back fourfold.
explain that everyone collects that way.
games.why: Zacchaeus stands and promises half his goods to the poor and fourfold to anyone he wronged. Jesus says salvation has come to that house.

practice: Bring to mind people who have been harmed by a church: someone you know, someone whose story you've read, maybe yourself, and let them be real to you without explaining their hurt away or rushing to defend anyone.

If you pray, hold them before God, by name or in silence, and ask for truth, justice and healing; if you don't, hold them in mind with respect. If you're being harmed now, call or text 988 in the US, or reach local emergency help.

wordCard.voice: When the church does wrong. The Bible's answer is honest confession, a turned life and real repair, beginning at the house of God.

orig.note: Greek: repentance — the word in "fruits meet for repentance" (Matthew 3:8).

carryVoice: Your line: repent. Zacchaeus didn't stop at sorry; he paid it back. See you tomorrow.
